title: Usage error exit when an option is repeated
description: Sources do not say what a repeated option does. Weighed: last wins vs usage error. Chose the narrower, stricter behavior.

options.label: Repeated option is a usage error (exit 2)

title: Half-up rounding implementation
description: Python round() is banker's rounding. Chose decimal.Decimal on the value's repr with ROUND_HALF_UP so 5.125 style values round up as the instructions require.

title: Fetch usage-error and file-write behavior
description: fetch with missing --start, --end, or --out, or an extra positional argument, is a usage error (exit 2). The output file is written only after the response validates, so failure never creates or alters a file.

title: Dispatch skeleton behaviour for registered commands
description: The spec says main consults COMMANDS for dispatch but defines no parser yet. A registered command name is accepted and main returns 0 without calling its handler, since Parsed does not exist until the options story. COMMANDS is typed Callable[[Any], str] to avoid importing a module that is not built yet. The options story should replace the placeholder with real dispatch. Is that acceptable?

title: Malformed feature handling
description: A feature missing id, properties, time, or coordinates raises OperationalError (exit 1) instead of a traceback. A null tsunami is read as 0, like a missing one. Is that acceptable?

title: Valid command with no registered handler
description: Until report handlers are registered in later blocks, a valid command such as summary exits 2 with 'command not available'. I chose a usage error over a silent success. The later blocks will replace this when they register handlers. Is that acceptable?

title: minmagnitude text
description: The spec says minmagnitude carries the text given on the command line. Parsed stores a float, so the fetch handler sends str(float). `--min-mag 5` therefore goes out as `5.0`. The declared ACs (4.5 and the 2.5 default) pass. Acceptable, or should Parsed keep the raw text?

title: Date validation
description: Dates must match YYYY-MM-DD and also be real calendar dates (2025-02-30 is a usage error). The spec only states the pattern. Is that acceptable?

title: Parser implementation and module
